overview: Black offers a pawn with 2...e5. After 3.dxe5 d4 4.Nf3 Nc6 Black has a space-gaining pawn on d4, a lead in development and ideas such as ...Bg4, ...Nge7-g6 and ...Bc5, while White tries to return the pawn at a good moment and consolidate with a3, g3 and Bg2. A classic trap is the Lasker trap (...Bg4 and ...Bb4+ ...dxc3 ...Bxc3+ lines). Objectively White keeps a small edge, but Black's play is active and tricky.

white_ideas.idea: Develop with Nf3, a3, g3, Bg2 and keep the extra pawn or return it for a safe position
Neutralise the d4 pawn with e3 and avoid the Lasker trap

black_ideas.idea: Keep the d4 pawn as a cramping wedge and develop with ...Nc6, ...Be6 or ...Bg4, ...Nge7
Attack with ...Bb4+ and ...dxc3 tricks and generate a kingside initiative

typical_structures.structure: Black pawn on d4 against White's c4, with White a pawn up and Black ahead in development

character.notes: Counter-gambit with a forcing, trappy opening and unbalanced positions; Sharp.

gambit.notes: After 3.dxe5 White can keep the pawn if he handles the development, as in the Albin anchor.

soundness.notes: Not refuted but White keeps an edge; I treat it as sound with moderate confidence.

structure.notes: Black pawn on d4 against White's e-pawn; d4 and c4 pawn wedge but the centre is fluid; Open.

approach.notes: An established gambit with real theory, played now and then by strong players; standard.

level.notes: Needs knowledge of traps and main lines; Intermediate for Black.

sublines_that_differ.name: 3.e3 (decline)
sublines_that_differ.how: Declined, no pawn changes hands, so no gambit.

character.reason: A counter-gambit that leads to unbalanced positions and tactics.

gambit.reason: Black gives a pawn that White can keep.

soundness.reason: White keeps a small edge but the gambit is not refuted.

structure.reason: A fluid, open centre with the d4 pawn clamp.

approach.reason: A recognised gambit with real theory, played now and then by strong players.

level.reason: Needs traps and main lines known.

plans.reason: Black plays for development and a d4 wedge.
